sentences.en: We are going to talk about something a little bit different today, a concept that you may or may not have heard of, which is toxic positivity.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊点稍微不同的话题，一个你可能听说过也可能没听过的概念，那就是有毒的正能量。

sentences.en: Even if you haven't heard of it, you've most likely experienced it in some form.
sentences.zh: 即使你没听说过这个词，你也多多少少经历过某种形式的有毒正能量。

sentences.en: People, you know, telling you to keep your chin up, that everything happens for a reason, to think good thoughts and they'll become your reality
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们会劝你振作起来，说什么一切发生皆有原因，只要心怀美好信念，它就会变成现实

sentences.en: because toxic positivity is everywhere these days, especially with the rise of a lot of Instagram and TikTok self-help content.
sentences.zh: 因为如今有毒的正能量无处不在，特别是随着大量Instagram和TikTok自我提升内容的兴起。

sentences.en: It is essentially this belief or this attitude that a positive mindset fixes everything.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一种信念或态度，即积极的心态能解决一切问题。

sentences.en: Whatever it is you're going through, being optimistic will make it better.
sentences.zh: 无论你经历着什么，保持乐观就能让事情变好。

sentences.en: And it's an attitude that has a lot of consequences for our mental health, for our emotional well-being, but also for our emotional intelligence
sentences.zh: 这种态度对我们的心理健康、情感福祉会产生很多负面影响，同时也会影响我们的情商

sentences.en: and our ability to actually address our emotions and solve our probleMs.
sentences.zh: 以及我们真正正视情绪和解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: I have to admit, I have been guilty of perhaps promoting this kind of messaging, both to myself and you guys, the listeners.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我自己也曾向听众朋友们以及自己传递过这种信息。

sentences.en: It is very easy to villainize negative emotions or so-called negative emotions because they simply just don't feel nice.
sentences.zh: 把负面情绪妖魔化，或者说所谓的负面情绪，是一件非常容易的事，因为它们给人的感觉确实不好受。

sentences.en: You know, feeling angry doesn't feel nice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，感到愤怒的感觉并不好受。

sentences.en: Feeling distressed, disappointed doesn't feel nice.
sentences.zh: 感到沮丧、失望的感觉也并不好受。

sentences.en: And putting a positive spin on things kind of erases the need to truly feel and process these big feelings.
sentences.zh: 而给事情强加一种积极的视角，在某种程度上就抹杀了真正去感受和处理这些强烈情绪的必要性。

sentences.en: But maturing is recognizing that just because something doesn't feel nice doesn't mean it's not useful.
sentences.zh: 但成熟意味着认识到，一件事情感觉不好并不代表它没有用。

sentences.en: And second to that, emotions like grief, like despair, like disappointment and rejection, they are what makes us human.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，悲伤、绝望、失望和拒绝这些情绪，正是它们构成了我们完整的人性。

sentences.en: And being able to connect with those emotions means that we are able to connect with ourselves, firstly, with our experiences, but also with others.
sentences.zh: 能够与这些情绪产生连接，意味着我们首先能够与自己连接，与我们的经历连接，同时也能够与他人连接。

sentences.en: It's a real privilege to sometimes not feel amazing all the time.
sentences.zh: 有时候并非无时无刻都感觉好极了，这其实是一种真正的特权。

sentences.en: Personally, I also think that toxic positivity is really dangerous during our 20s in particular because, you know, our emotions can teach us so much during this period
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我也认为有毒的正能量在我们的二十岁尤其危险，因为你知道，在这段时期我们的情绪能教给我们太多东西

sentences.en: and they do influence who we are becoming.
sentences.zh: 并且它们确实在影响着我们正在成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: So if we mask them by being overly positive about everything, by not letting anything in, by numbing ourselves out, we're kind of doing ourselves a disservice.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们通过对每件事都过度乐观来掩盖情绪，不让任何真实感受进来，把自己的感知麻木掉，我们其实是在害了自己。

sentences.en: And it may sound strange to hear me say that, you know, being too positive is a danger to you is dangerous because how can something so nice be so dangerous?
sentences.zh: 听到我说“过于积极对你来说是一种危险，是危险的”可能会觉得奇怪，因为这么美好的东西怎么会这么危险呢？

sentences.en: But when we gravitate towards the same reaction for all of our experiences, i.e. always looking for the bright side, no matter how hard or difficult something is,
sentences.zh: 但当我们对所有的经历都倾向于做出相同的反应，即无论事情多么艰难困苦，总是寻找光明的一面时

sentences.en: we do tend to suppress a lot of what makes us so tender and so unique and so vulnerable and that vulnerability is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会压抑许多让我们变得如此温柔、独特和脆弱的东西，而这种脆弱其实是一件好事。

sentences.en: So today we are going to discuss the problem with always being positive.

sentences.en: And I know it sounds strange, but why feeling bad is sometimes good for you.

sentences.en: We'll also dive into why it is that we tend to gravitate towards optimism, this concept of self-inflicted emotional gaslighting and the alternative.

sentences.en: Toxic positivity has a few different names.
sentences.zh: 有毒的正能量有几个不同的名字。

sentences.en: You know, the first time that it was labelled was back in the 1980s and back then it was known as unrealistic optimism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在20世纪80年代第一次被命名时，被称为不切实际的乐观主义。

sentences.en: It's also known as bright-siding, positive tyranny, which is very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 它也被称为“只看光明面”（bright-siding）和“积极暴政”（positive tyranny），这个名字听起来非常戏剧化。

sentences.en: But I think you get the picture.
sentences.zh: 但我想你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, all these terms are referring to the same thing.
sentences.zh: 说到底，所有这些术语指的都是同一件事。

sentences.en: A deep but also toxic and maladaptive belief that thinking positively can erase all negative feelings and that those negative feelings are bad.
sentences.zh: 一种根深蒂固但又充满毒性和适应不良的信念，即积极思考可以抹去所有负面情绪，并且那些负面情绪是坏事。

sentences.en: We have bad emotions that we should not feel and the way to not feel them is to cover them in sugar and cover them in sunshine
sentences.zh: 我们有一些不应该感受的坏情绪，而消除这些情绪的方法就是把它们裹上糖衣，洒满阳光

sentences.en: and always find the positive, always try and shake it off.
sentences.zh: 永远去寻找积极的一面，总是试着把它甩掉。

sentences.en: We want to prioritise upbeat thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们想要优先考虑乐观向上的思维。

sentences.en: We want to push down the difficult stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们要把那些困难的东西压抑下去。

sentences.en: No one wants to see that.
sentences.zh: 没有人想看到那一面。

sentences.en: No one wants to feel that.
sentences.zh: 没有人想去感受那种情绪。

sentences.en: And if you can't be positive all the time, you have somehow failed.
sentences.zh: 如果你不能一直保持积极，那你就是某种程度上的失败者。

sentences.en: Something is wrong with you.
sentences.zh: 你身上出了问题。

sentences.en: This can be a belief that we've learned from someone else around us or it can be self-imposed, like feeling guilty when you feel sad or disappointed
sentences.zh: 这种信念可能是我们从身边的某个人那里学来的，也可能是我们自己强加给自己的，比如当你感到悲伤或失望时会感到内疚

sentences.en: and immediately forcing yourself to think about everything you should be grateful for instead of letting yourself be sad or pushing down big feelings
sentences.zh: 然后立刻强迫自己去想所有你本该感恩的事情，而不是让自己去悲伤，或者通过告诉自己“情况可能更糟糕”来压抑强烈的感受

sentences.en: by telling yourself it could be worse.
sentences.zh: 然后就此翻篇。

sentences.en: Just move on.
sentences.zh: 继续往前走就行了。

sentences.en: This is why toxic positivity is sometimes seen as a form of self-inflicted emotional gaslighting.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有毒的正能量有时被视为一种自我施加的情感操纵形式。

sentences.en: That is a mouthful, but I think we're all pretty familiar with the term gaslighting when it comes to romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 这个词有点拗口，但我想我们对恋爱关系中的“操纵”（gaslighting）这个词都相当熟悉。

sentences.en: It's this act of one person manipulating somebody else into questioning their own reality and what is actually true or real as a way to maintain control over them.
sentences.zh: 这是一种行为，一个人操纵另一个人去质疑他们自己的现实以及什么是真实存在的，以此来对他们保持控制。

sentences.en: When we force ourselves to push down and push aside hard emotions, the premise is that we are essentially gaslighting ourselves by saying this isn't real.
sentences.zh: 当我们强迫自己压抑和推开艰难的情绪时，其前提本质上就是我们在对自己进行情感操纵，对自己说这一切都不是真实的。

sentences.en: You don't know what you're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道自己在经历什么。

sentences.en: You're choosing to feel bad about this rather than you feel bad about this because it's hard and that's a normal reaction.
sentences.zh: 你这是选择为此感到难过，而不是承认你感到难过是因为事情很难，而这是一种正常的反应。

sentences.en: This experience is real and raw and it's okay to be in pain and to be flat for a while.
sentences.zh: 这种经历是真实而深刻的，感到痛苦并在一段时间内情绪低落是没有问题的。

sentences.en: This is hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: You can feel sad about it.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以为此感到难过。

sentences.en: More often than not though, toxic positivity is something that we experience from others.
sentences.zh: 不过，更多时候，有毒的正能量是我们从别人身上体验到的。

sentences.en: There is of course that own sense of like almost self-preservation I would call it to maintain a positive outlook at all times
sentences.zh: 当然，我们自身也有一种几乎可以说是为了在任何时候都保持乐观心态的自我保护意识

sentences.en: but there are often these times when perhaps you go to a therapist or a family member or a friend and you say, you know, I'm just really struggling with this thing.
sentences.zh: 但往往会有这样的时候，也许你去找心理医生、家人或朋友倾诉，你说，你知道的，我真的在苦恼这件事。

sentences.en: This terrible thing is happening.
sentences.zh: 这件糟糕的事正在发生。

sentences.en: I'm really stressed.

sentences.en: I'm really tired.
sentences.zh: 我太累了。

sentences.en: I'm really exhausted
sentences.zh: 我筋疲力尽

sentences.en: and the only thing they try and do is get you to see the positive sides.
sentences.zh: 而他们唯一试图做的就是让你看到积极的一面。

sentences.en: They only try and get you to see the light at the end of the tunnel
sentences.zh: 他们只想让你看到隧道尽头的曙光

sentences.en: and I get it.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: I really do get why a family member or a friend or a therapist or anybody would want to bring us back to what is good because we don't like to see other people struggle.
sentences.zh: 我真的明白为什么家人、朋友、心理医生或任何人会想要把我们带回好的方面，因为我们都不喜欢看别人挣扎。

sentences.en: We don't like to see other people feel sad, especially people that we love.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢看别人感到悲伤，尤其是我们爱的人。

sentences.en: You know, some examples of this are like when you go through a breakup and you're immediately told that, you know, there's someone better out there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这方面的一些例子比如当你经历分手时，别人立刻告诉你，你知道的，外面有更好的人。

sentences.en: Think about the positives in the situation.
sentences.zh: 想想这种情况积极的一面吧。

sentences.en: Think about how fun it's going to be single when you perhaps aren't ready to hear that.
sentences.zh: 想想当你可能还没准备好听到这些时，单身会有多有趣。

sentences.en: Losing your job and being told that, you know, you could have it worse.
sentences.zh: 失业时别人告诉你，你知道的，你的情况还算好的。

sentences.en: Some people don't even have a job.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至连工作都没有。

sentences.en: Some people don't even have a savings.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至连存款都没有。

sentences.en: Some people have been unemployed so much longer than you.
sentences.zh: 有些人失业的时间比你长得多。

sentences.en: So chin up.
sentences.zh: 所以振作点吧。

sentences.en: It's all that line of thinking, you know, getting ghosted, getting rejected and being told that everything happens for a reason.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种思维模式，遭遇冷暴力、被拒绝时，别人告诉你一切发生皆有原因。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a nice thought.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个美好的想法。

sentences.en: It just might not be helpful.
sentences.zh: 只是它可能并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: And it's probably one of those thoughts that's only helpful in hindsight when you're ready to hear it.
sentences.zh: 而且这可能是一种只有在事后、当你准备好接受时才会有帮助的想法。

sentences.en: What's another example that we see a lot?
sentences.zh: 我们经常看到的另一个例子是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, somebody was telling me about this the other day.
sentences.zh: 哦，前几天有人跟我提起过这个。

sentences.en: Like when you go and like see a friend or you're with a family member or whoever it is and you just feel like you can't be low energy because they'll immediately pathologize
sentences.zh: 比如当你去见一个朋友，或者和家人在一起，无论对方是谁，你只是觉得自己不能表现出低能量，因为他们会立刻给它贴上病态的标签

sentences.en: or think that something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 或者认为你出了什么问题。

sentences.en: So if you're like, oh, I've just had a really bad day, they'll immediately be like, well, that's not good.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你说，天哪，我今天过得真糟透了，他们马上就会说，嗯，那可不太好。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: We don't want you to have a bad day.
sentences.zh: 我们可不想让你过得不开心。

sentences.en: Let's make this better.
sentences.zh: 让我们把事情弄好点。

sentences.en: We need to think positively.
sentences.zh: 我们需要积极地思考。

sentences.en: We need to fix your problem when you might just be having a bad day
sentences.zh: 当你的确只是碰上糟糕的一天时，我们需要帮你解决问题，

sentences.en: or overemphasizing the power of gratitude.
sentences.zh: 或者过度强调感恩的力量。

sentences.en: That is something that we see all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是我们经常看到的一种现象。

sentences.en: I had an example from a friend.
sentences.zh: 我有一个朋友的例子。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, from a friend, an acquaintance who was telling me about how one of her co-workers lost her mother to cancer really unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对，是一个朋友，一个熟人，她跟我说起她的一个同事如何非常突然地因癌症失去了母亲。

sentences.en: And of course, dealing with that just humongous grief, unimaginable grief, she went and saw a therapist and the therapist, or it was a counselor, told her to make a gratitude list
sentences.zh: 当然，为了应付那种巨大的悲伤，那种难以想象的悲伤，她去看了一位治疗师，而治疗师，或者说是个顾问，让她列一个感恩清单

sentences.en: to help her feel better.
sentences.zh: 来帮助她感觉好一点。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I get that her intentions were most likely in the right place, but you can also see how this is probably not helpful.
sentences.zh: 我明白对方的初衷很可能是好的，但你也能看出这大概并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: That's probably not the one thing that we need to do.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是我们唯一需要做的事情。

sentences.en: This is almost a denial of the negative emotions
sentences.zh: 这几乎是对负面情绪的一种否定，

sentences.en: and an unrealistic promotion of positive thinking when this person probably would actually not benefit from immediately moving on.
sentences.zh: 也是对积极思维的不切实际的推崇，而此时这个人其实并不会因为马上往前看而受益。

sentences.en: That's what I get the point of like, oh yeah, what are you grateful for?
sentences.zh: 这就是我的意思，比如，哦对了，你对什么心怀感恩？

sentences.en: So you don't dwell on this loss, but maybe it would have been better to just be like, yeah, that's really, really awful.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会纠结于这种失落，但也许更好的做法是直接说，嗯，这真的很糟糕、很糟糕。

sentences.en: That really sucks.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人难受。

sentences.en: Let's just let you feel really bad about that for a while because that is a completely reasonable thing to be feeling.
sentences.zh: 让我们就让你为此难过上一阵子吧，因为这是一种完全合理的感受。

sentences.en: One final example, because I'm filled with anecdotes today, is this experience, this concept I don't know what it is, a term known as bright siding.
sentences.zh: 最后一个例子，因为我今天满脑子都是轶事，就是这种体验，这个概念——我不知道它到底是什么，一个被称为“积极向阳（bright siding）”的词。

sentences.en: And we see this a lot when someone tells us a story about something really frustrating or really terrible or painful,
sentences.zh: 当有人给我们讲述一件非常令人沮丧、非常糟糕或痛苦的事情时，我们经常会看到这种现象，

sentences.en: and immediately somebody else jumps in with a matching story of their own that is far more terrible and far more painful.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个人会立刻插话，讲一个他们自己的、更加糟糕也更加痛苦的匹配故事。

sentences.en: Or they point out the one part of the story where something good happened or something worse could have happened.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会指出故事中发生好事的那一部分，或是原本可能发生更糟糕情况的那一部分。

sentences.en: You know, oh, I just had the most terrible commute to work today.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，哦，我今天通勤去上班简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I was so frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我太沮丧了。

sentences.en: I was so angry by the time I got in.
sentences.zh: 当我到达公司时，我已经气炸了。

sentences.en: I just like didn't want to be there.
sentences.zh: 我简直不想待在那里。

sentences.en: And then they go, well, on the bright side, like at least, you know, what happened to me today?
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说，好吧，从积极的一面来看，至少，你知道，我今天经历了什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, at least, you know, your car didn't explode like mine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少，你知道，你的车不像我的那样爆炸了。

sentences.en: So you have something to feel good about.
sentences.zh: 所以你有什么好觉得欣慰的。

sentences.en: It's like, well, when that happens, it immediately kind of cuts off your ability to express your feelings because you either feel the need to justify the experience
sentences.zh: 这就好比，当这种情况发生时，它会立刻在某种程度上切断你表达感受的能力，因为要么你会觉得有必要为主观体验辩解，

sentences.en: or you can't compete and therefore you just go quiet.
sentences.zh: 要么你无法与之竞争，因此只能选择沉默。

sentences.en: And there is this incredible book about this exact concept called Bright Sided, how the relentless promotion of positive thinking has undermined America.
sentences.zh: 有一本关于这个确切概念的了不起的书，叫做《积极的祸害（Bright Sided）》，讲述了对积极思维的不懈推崇是如何毁掉美国的。

sentences.en: And it talks about how by stamping out negative thoughts or villainizing negative emotions, we become very two-dimensional.
sentences.zh: 它探讨了通过消除消极思想或将负面情绪妖魔化，我们是如何变得非常扁平化的。

sentences.en: We learn pretty quickly that actually being truthful, looking for comfort rather than solutions or optimism is going to be met with toxic positivity.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会明白，实际上，实话实说、寻求安慰而不是解决方案或盲目乐观，会遭到有毒的积极性（toxic positivity）的回击。

sentences.en: So eventually, we just become our happy moments.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，我们只展现我们快乐的时刻。

sentences.en: We just show people the good things and everyone looks at each other thinking, wow, her life is really perfect.
sentences.zh: 我们只把美好的一面展示给别人看，每个人看着彼此，心里都在想，哇，她的生活真的很完美。

sentences.en: Her life is really amazing.
sentences.zh: 她的生活真的很精彩。

sentences.en: Whilst you think the same thing about them.
sentences.zh: 同时你对他们也是这么想的。

sentences.en: And essentially, the author makes this very convincing argument that toxic positivity has made us inauthentic.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，作者提出了一个非常有说服力的论点，即有毒的积极性让我们变得虚伪不真诚。

sentences.en: And I tend to agree.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于赞同这一点。

sentences.en: Let me play devil's advocate for a second before we fully jump into the consequences of this.
sentences.zh: 在我们完全深入探讨这一现象的后果之前，让我先扮演一会儿魔鬼的代言人。

sentences.en: You know, we do see toxic positivity everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们到处都能看到有毒的积极性。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 而且你知道吗？

sentences.en: Sometimes it is only natural to want to see the bright side of what we're going through.
sentences.zh: 有时，想要看到我们所经历事情积极的一面，纯粹是人之常情。

sentences.en: It can be useful and it can also be intuitive.
sentences.zh: 它既有用，也很符合直觉。

sentences.en: As humans, both, you know, evolutionarily, but also socially, we naturally prefer positive emotions.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，无论是从演化角度还是从社会角度来看，我们都天生地偏爱积极的情绪。

sentences.en: They indicate greater happiness, greater satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 它们预示着更大的幸福和更大的满足感。

sentences.en: They create less emotional pain and disharmony, less social friction.
sentences.zh: 它们带来的情感痛苦和不和谐更少，社交摩擦也更少。

sentences.en: We would probably prefer to not get bogged down in hard things.
sentences.zh: 我们或许更愿意不被艰难的事情所拖累。

sentences.en: There are also just people who are really optimistic.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人本身就是真正的乐天派。

sentences.en: It's not that they're necessarily toxic in their optimism.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们的乐观必然是有毒的。

sentences.en: It's just how they come.
sentences.zh: 这只是他们的天性使然。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people would probably look at that, those explanations that I just gave of people trying their hardest to relate to somebody else through a positive lens
sentences.zh: 我想很多人看到我刚才给出的那些解释——即人们竭尽全力通过积极的视角去与他人共情——可能会觉得，

sentences.en: and be like, what's the problem?
sentences.zh: 这有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: What's the problem here?
sentences.zh: 这儿有什么问题？

sentences.en: Of course, it's better to be happy than sad.
sentences.zh: 当然，开心总比难过好。

sentences.en: You know, of course, this lightens the mood.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这当然能活跃气氛。

sentences.en: People want to be around you.
sentences.zh: 大家都愿意和你待在一起。

sentences.en: People want to be your friend.
sentences.zh: 大家都想和你做朋友。

sentences.en: People want to be happy.
sentences.zh: 人人都想快乐。

sentences.en: And I really do understand that.
sentences.zh: 我确实理解这一点。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that in these instances, there isn't room for resilience.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说在这些情况下，就没有韧性存在的空间了。

sentences.en: There isn't room for gratitude.
sentences.zh: 没有感恩的空间。

sentences.en: There isn't room for problem solving.
sentences.zh: 没有解决问题的空间。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that those things are healthy coping mechanisms when we overly rely on them, when our solution to anything bad is just be grateful for what you have or, okay,
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，当我们将这些东西作为健康的应对机制却过度依赖它们时，当我们对任何糟糕事情的解决办法只是“感恩你所拥有的”或者“好吧，

sentences.en: just get over it and keep your chin up.
sentences.zh: 振作起来，向前看”时，

sentences.en: That is toxic positivity versus healthy positivity.
sentences.zh: 这就是有毒的积极性与健康积极性的区别。

sentences.en: These happy good vibes become toxic when it involves avoiding and suppressing, minimizing or rejecting negative feelings.
sentences.zh: 当这些快乐的美好氛围涉及回避、压抑、淡化或排斥负面情绪时，它们就变得有毒了。

sentences.en: And let's be real, that doesn't actually make them go away.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这并不能真正让它们消失。

sentences.en: That doesn't allow us to make peace with them.
sentences.zh: 这并不能让我们与它们达成和解。

sentences.en: The only thing that is occurring is that in the moment, they become invisible.
sentences.zh: 唯一发生的事情是，在当下，它们变得隐形了。

sentences.en: And that means that eventually, they will most likely return with a vengeance later on.
sentences.zh: 这意味着最终它们极有可能会在以后卷土重来。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the consequences of toxic positivity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来谈谈有毒积极性的后果。

sentences.en: First of all, it stigmatizes these so-called negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 首先，它给这些所谓的负面情绪贴上了污名化的标签。

sentences.en: And I know that I've been using that word very, that term very frequently, negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 我知道我一直在频繁使用这个词、这个术语——负面情绪。

sentences.en: Basically, what I mean by that is the emotions that are very much villainized by society.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我指的是那些被社会极度妖魔化的情绪。

sentences.en: Things that we kind of cringe at, we would rather not see.
sentences.zh: 那些我们觉得有点难为情、宁愿看不见的东西。

sentences.en: Anger, jealousy, grief, sadness.
sentences.zh: 愤怒、嫉妒、悲伤、哀痛。

sentences.en: Often, the reason that these emotions, I think, are so disturbing to some people is because they are so human.
sentences.zh: 通常，我认为这些情绪之所以让某些人感到如此不安，是因为它们是如此地具有人性。

sentences.en: And when we see somebody else experiencing them, we so deeply
sentences.zh: 当我们看到别人经历这些时，我们能够极其深刻地

sentences.en: can see ourselves in that feeling.
sentences.zh: 在那种感觉中看到我们自己。

sentences.en: We know what that feels like and I think that kind of makes us feel embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那是什么感觉，我认为这让我们感到有些尴尬。

sentences.en: Like, oh, don't be loud about what it means to be human.
sentences.zh: 就像是在说，噢，别把人性的这面表现得太大声。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: sometimes being human is just kind of shit.
sentences.zh: 有时候作为人就是有点糟糕。

sentences.en: Sometimes it just isn't fun.
sentences.zh: 有时候就是一点都不好玩。

sentences.en: There is not a single person alive today who would say, you know, my entire life has been golden.
sentences.zh: 当今活着的没有一个人会说，你知道的，我的一生全是金色的。

sentences.en: Everything is great for me.
sentences.zh: 我的一切都好极了。

sentences.en: And yet, it feels like that is what is kind of expected.
sentences.zh: 然而，这似乎正是人们所期望的。

sentences.en: These negative emotions,
sentences.zh: 这些负面情绪，

sentences.en: they are what keep us from being a very palatable person, from being somebody who always leaves others feeling in a good mood.
sentences.zh: 它们正是让我们免于成为一个过于随和的人、免于成为一个总是让别人感觉心情大好的人的屏障。

sentences.en: If nothing else, these negative emotions, I actually think are really useful because they make our good moments and our good memories even more special.
sentences.zh: 退一步讲，我实际上认为这些负面情绪真的很有用，因为它们让我们的美好时刻和美好记忆变得更加特别。

sentences.en: They are also a natural reaction to our experiences and they teach us something, they have a purpose.
sentences.zh: 它们也是对我们经历的自然反应，它们能教给我们一些东西，它们有其存在的目的。

sentences.en: And I think our desire to hide them links very closely to the stigma that is directed towards mental health and mental health conditions and mental health struggles.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们隐藏它们的渴望，与针对心理健康、心理健康状况以及心理健康斗争的污名紧密相连。

sentences.en: And I don't think that that is an accident.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一个巧合。

sentences.en: Society is not that great at wanting people to be open about what they're going through.
sentences.zh: 社会并不那么擅长希望人们对自己的经历坦诚相待。

sentences.en: There is a long history of that.
sentences.zh: 这有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: And if we've never been taught to accept that this is a dimension of being human, if we continue to keep up this narrative that intense emotions deserve to be hidden, they deserve
sentences.zh: 如果我们从未被教导去接受这是人性的一部分，如果我们继续维持这种叙事，即强烈的情绪活该被隐藏、活该

sentences.en: to be masked by optimism or masked by positivity, the next generation is taught the same thing.
sentences.zh: 被乐观主义或积极性所掩盖，那么下一代受到的教育也会是一模一样。

sentences.en: And that is where prejudice and misunderstanding comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是偏见和误解的来源。

sentences.en: A failure to really normalise and accept what is typical for most people which is that we do feel sad and we do feel angry and we do grieve and that doesn't always need to be
sentences.zh: 无法真正正常化并接受大多数人的典型状态——也就是我们确实会感到难过、会感到愤怒、会感到悲伤，而这并不总是需要被

sentences.en: stamped out.
sentences.zh: 根除。

sentences.en: It makes us feel like we always have to be okay when no one is and I saw this quote about this from an author that said this unrealistic optimism towards life is essentially saying
sentences.zh: 它让我们觉得，当没有谁真正一切都好时，我们却必须表现得一切都好。我看到一位作家的一句名言说，这种对生活不切实际的乐观主义，本质上是在说

sentences.en: whatever you do don't tell the truth of what it is like to be alive.
sentences.zh: 无论你做什么，千万别说出活着到底是什么滋味。

sentences.en: Don't be authentic, don't be honest, don't be open.
sentences.zh: 不要真实，不要诚实，不要坦诚。

sentences.en: It's like having a nice illusion of what everything should look like.
sentences.zh: 这就好比对万物本该呈现的样子抱有一种美好的幻想。

sentences.en: It's, I don't know, it's not that there is like this greater power that is controlling this and making everyone, forcing them to look happy.
sentences.zh: 这，我不知道，并不是说有什么强大的力量在控制着这一切，让每个人都强颜欢笑。

sentences.en: It is like a long pattern and a long history of this going on and I think it mainly comes down to the effects of shame and embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一种长期存在的模式和悠久的历史，我认为这主要归结为羞耻感和尴尬感的影响。

sentences.en: We aren't, you know, necessarily coming out and saying
sentences.zh: 我们并不是，你知道的，直接走出来说

sentences.en: ew, why are you crying?
sentences.zh: 咦，你为什么在哭？

sentences.en: Don't be upset, that makes me so uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 别难过了，这让我很不舒服。

sentences.en: You know, we aren't being like can you please stop that?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们并不是表现得好像“你能别这样吗？”

sentences.en: Can you please stop grieving all over the place or stop being, like, stop being, you know, upset all over the place?
sentences.zh: “你能别到处悲伤吗？或者别，别，你知道的，到处难过吗？”

sentences.en: Like, no, stop.
sentences.zh: 就像，不，住手。
